subject: Music Production
title: The Rise of 78 RPM Records
description: A 60-second lesson on The Rise of 78 RPM Records.

hook.text: By the 1910s, the industry settled on 78 revolutions per minute as the standard disc speed.

buildup.text: Each side of a 78 RPM disc held only about three to four minutes of music.

discovery.text: This time limit forced songwriters to keep compositions short, shaping pop music structure.

twist.text: Classical labels solved the limit by selling multiple discs bundled in book-like packages.

climax.text: Those multi-disc packages gave us the word 'album,' still used for music collections today.

punchline.text: A time limit on shellac created the pop song format.

quiz.question: How did the 78 RPM time limit influence music?
options: It forced songs to be kept short
